scope: DCP-LETT-2156 missing query list and DCP-LETT-2157 date assessment; no source, packet, projection, accepted-ledger, or export mutation.

findings.conclusion: No complete authoritative public transcription located.

evidence.quote: This is CD’s ‘list of queries’ referred to in the letter. It is preserved in DAR 114: 222c.

findings.extent: The DCP page preserves only 2156 body paragraph 13 (“I have just looked at my list of queries...”) and footnote references to Adlumia, yaks, Linum and DAR 114:222c. Search found no public image or full text of the sheet itself. The DCP alternate editorial endpoint and Darwin Online catalogue confirm custody/reference only; they do not supply the missing list.
findings.limit: Do not admit the query list as a transcript or synthesize its questions from footnote topics.

findings.conclusion: 23 October 1857 remains the best supported editorial date, but it is not an independently surviving dateline.

evidence.quote: on that day (Oct 31) for Etty who is coming home.
it will reach there on Saturday Evening

findings.reasoning: The footnote explicitly derives 23 October from “the Friday preceding 31 October 1857”; 23 is the prior Friday, while 30 is the immediately preceding day and would make Saturday delivery coincide with Etty’s 31 October return. The body’s Saturday dispatch/late-dinner arrangements fit the 23→24 October week better. Preserve the editorial 23 October assignment and flag it as derived, not a handwritten date; do not silently replace it with 30 October.
findings.limit: No surviving independent postmark or dateline was located in the preserved HTML.

notes: Public research was used only to locate provenance; no remote text was downloaded or incorporated as a transcript.
The missing DAR 114:222c list remains a bounded unresolved input.
